label: Ruckus R750 Wi-Fi 6 indoor access point
description: Ruckus R750 - dual-band dual-concurrent Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) access point for ultra-dense indoor spaces: 8 spatial streams (4x4:4 in both bands), up to 1024 clients, BeamFlex+ adaptive antennas, onboard BLE and Zigbee IoT radios, one 2.5Gbps and one 1Gbps Ethernet port with 802.3af/at/bt PoE, a USB 2.0 port, 4 to 2400 Mbps 802.11ax rates.
notes: Source is CommScope/Ruckus's own **HTML datasheet** (`webresources.ruckuswireless.com/datasheets/<slug>/ds-ruckus-<slug>.html`), whose **PHYSICAL INTERFACES** table is machine-readable text - the 4gon product pages for these APs return no extractable content and the AP pages on ruckusnetworks.com are script-driven. **Two Ethernet ports of different speeds, and the fast one is the uplink:** 'Ethernet: One 2.5Gbps Ethernet port and one 1Gbps Ethernet port - Power over Ethernet (802.3af/at/bt) with Category 5/5e/6 cable - LLDP', confirmed by the ordering row: 'dual ports ... One Ethernet port is 2.5GbE'. **Three PoE classes:** af, at *and* bt, with the datasheet's consumption figures - 12.54 W on 802.3af, 22.34 W on 802.3at+, 22.69 W on DC - so the spec carries all three classes rather than the highest, and an 802.3af injector is a legal way to power it at reduced capability. **Radios carry no per-band rate:** the rate row is a single '802.11ax: 4 to 2400 Mbps', so inventing a 2.4 GHz figure from the 4x4:4 stream count would be my arithmetic. 1024 clients, 8 spatial streams, onboard BLE and Zigbee (IoT radios are not Ethernet and are not modelled).
